prompt:
Add a `tasklist` extension: a list item whose text starts with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` followed by a space becomes a task.
- The marker is replaced by `<input type="checkbox">`, `checked` for `x`/`X`, and `disabled` unless the `clickable` option is true (default false).
- The `<li>` gets the class from the `item_class` option (default `task`).
- It works in ordered and unordered lists, nested lists and loose lists, and keeps inline markup after the marker.
Register it so `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` works once installed.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
I added the `tasklist` extension, and `markdown.Markdown(extensions=['tasklist'])` loads it by short name. It turns list items starting with `[ ]`, `[x]` or `[X]` plus a space into tasks. It works in ordered, unordered, nested and loose lists and keeps inline markup after the marker. The new tests (14) and the full suite pass; flake8 and the spell check were not run because they are not installed here.

- The checkbox is `checked` for `x`/`X` and `disabled` unless `clickable=True`; the `<li>` gets the `item_class` class (default `task`), and an empty `item_class` adds no class.
- The space after the marker stays in the output (`<input ... /> Task`) so the checkbox and text don't run together.
- The marker is read before links are processed, so `[x]` still becomes a checkbox when the document also defines a link reference named `x`.
- Not treated as tasks: `[ ]` with nothing after it, `[x]Text`, `[y] Text`, an escaped `\[x] ` and a marker in the middle of the text.

The entry point is registered in both `pyproject.toml` and the fixture's `entry_points.txt`. Following the contributing guide, I also added a docs page, an API reference stub, entries in the extensions index and site navigation, an `[unreleased]` changelog entry with no issue number (there isn't one), and three words in `.spell-dict`.
